section: Nature and scope of ICT; basics of hardware, software, memory and operating systems
subsections: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units
Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers
Software types - system, application, utility, open-source
Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples
Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of digital information units from smaller to larger, excluding the units already commonly used for basic computer measurements?
accepted.x: The larger units follow the sequence PB, EB, ZB and YB; therefore EB < ZB < YB is correct.
accepted.tq: Test the numerical sequence by comparing adjacent units.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A nibble in computer terminology consists of
accepted.x: A nibble is a group of four bits.
accepted.tq: Recall the fixed-size relationship between binary storage units.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about RAM is correct?
o: It is slower than magnetic tape.
It is temporary working memory and is volatile.
It is erased only by ultraviolet light.
accepted.x: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use and loses its contents when power is removed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish volatile working memory from non-volatile storage.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SRAM is used in cache memory.
2. DRAM is commonly used as main memory.
3. Both SRAM and DRAM are types of ROM.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SRAM is associated with cache and DRAM with main memory. Statement 3 is false because both are forms of RAM.
accepted.tq: Identify the single wrong classification in a set of related memory statements.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which type of ROM can be erased using ultraviolet light?
accepted.x: EPROM is erased by exposure to ultraviolet light, whereas EEPROM is erased electrically.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar memory technologies by their erasure methods.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: EEPROM — erasable only by ultraviolet light
accepted.x: EPROM is erased using ultraviolet light. EEPROM is electrically erasable, while ROM is non-volatile.
accepted.tq: Use the exact technical distinction among closely related memory terms.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in descending order of access speed:
A. RAM
B. Registers
C. Magnetic tape
D. Cache
accepted.x: The speed order is registers, cache, RAM and magnetic tape.
accepted.tq: Arrange items by performance hierarchy, beginning with the fastest.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of a solid-state drive?
o: It uses flash memory and has no moving parts.
It uses a blue-violet laser to read data.
accepted.x: An SSD uses flash memory, has no moving parts and is generally faster than an HDD.
accepted.tq: Separate storage devices by their underlying technology.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which storage medium is primarily associated with sequential access and archival backup?
accepted.x: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access medium commonly used for backup and archival purposes.
accepted.tq: Match a storage medium with its characteristic use.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the approximate single-layer capacity?
1. CD — 700 MB
2. DVD — 4.7 GB
3. Blu-ray — 25 GB
accepted.x: A single-layer CD stores about 700 MB, a single-layer DVD about 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray disc about 25 GB.
accepted.tq: Check all numerical pairings before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Blu-ray discs use which type of laser?
accepted.x: Blu-ray technology uses a blue-violet laser to read and write data.
accepted.tq: Recall the device-specific technology rather than the general category.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A flash drive or memory card is primarily based on
accepted.x: Pen drives and memory cards use EEPROM-based flash memory.
accepted.tq: Match portable storage devices with their internal technology.
accepted.sec: Memory and storage - primary vs secondary, capacities, storage units  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following devices can function as both an input and an output device?
accepted.x: A touch screen displays output and also receives input through touch.
accepted.tq: Apply the input-output classification to a dual-function device.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Device)
a. Barcode reader
a. OCR
b. MICR
c. OMR

List-II (Primary use)
i. Reading marked answer sheets
ii. Reading characters printed with magnetic ink
iii. Reading machine-readable bars
iv. Converting printed or handwritten text into editable text

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Barcode readers read bars, MICR reads magnetic-ink characters, OMR reads marked sheets and OCR converts text into editable form.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong reader-function pair.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A barcode is best described as
o: a printed image converted into editable text
a two-dimensional matrix of square modules
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
a magnetic character sequence used on cheques
accepted.x: A conventional barcode consists of machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths.
accepted.tq: Distinguish barcode, QR code, OCR and MICR by physical form and function.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit of a CPU primarily performs
accepted.x: The ALU performs arithmetic calculations and logical operations.
accepted.tq: Match each CPU component with its specific responsibility.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about CPU components:
1. The control unit fetches and decodes instructions.
2. Registers are very fast storage locations inside the CPU.
3. The power supply unit directs the execution of program instructions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The control unit fetches, decodes and directs operations, while registers provide very fast internal storage. The PSU supplies power and does not direct instruction execution.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement assigning a CPU control function to a power-supply component.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: The motherboard primarily performs which function?
o: It converts printed text into editable text.
It permanently stores all user files.
It links the major components of a computer.
accepted.x: The motherboard provides the principal connections among the computer's components.
accepted.tq: Identify the central hardware interconnection component.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first commercial microprocessor?
accepted.x: The Intel 4004, introduced in 1971, was the first commercial microprocessor.
accepted.tq: Link the historical milestone with the specific processor model.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: Which processor technology is especially suited to graphics processing and several artificial-intelligence workloads?
accepted.x: Graphics processing units are designed for highly parallel computations used in graphics and many AI workloads.
accepted.tq: Infer the processor type from the stated computational application.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a non-impact printer?
accepted.x: Laser printers are non-impact printers; dot-matrix, daisy-wheel and line printers are impact printers.
accepted.tq: Separate printer classes by whether the print mechanism strikes the paper.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: Printer quality and speed are commonly expressed, respectively, in
accepted.x: Print quality is measured in dots per inch (dpi), while speed may be expressed in pages per minute (ppm).
accepted.tq: Match measurement units with the correct printer performance parameter.
accepted.sec: Hardware - input vs output, CPU components, processors, readers, printers  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is utility software rather than application software?
accepted.x: Antivirus software is a utility designed to maintain or protect the computer system.
accepted.tq: Distinguish software by its primary purpose rather than by its interface.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Operating system — system software
2. Disk cleanup — utility software
3. Word processor — application software
4. Device driver — application software
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified. A device driver is system software, so pair 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrongly classified software category.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of application software?
accepted.x: A compiler is a language translator and therefore system software; the other three are application programs.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by separating system tools from end-user applications.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement best describes open-source software?
o: It is limited to operating systems produced by one company.
Its source code is permanently hidden from users.
It can never be commercially distributed.
Its source code is free to view, modify and share, subject to its licence.
accepted.x: Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the precise definition.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Richard Stallman initiated the GNU project in 1983. Linus Torvalds developed the Linux kernel in 1991.
accepted.tq: Use the person-project-year trap to distinguish related open-source milestones.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an open-source software product?
accepted.x: LibreOffice is an example of open-source software; Firefox is another example.
accepted.tq: Identify a product from the open-source software category.
accepted.sec: Software types - system, application, utility, open-source  [GK]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT a normal responsibility of an operating system?
1. Managing hardware
2. Handling processes and memory
3. Managing files and device drivers
4. Manufacturing the motherboard
accepted.x: An operating system manages hardware resources, processes, memory, files and drivers. Manufacturing a motherboard is not an operating-system function.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated function among genuine operating-system responsibilities.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An operating system used for missile guidance, air-traffic control or a medical device generally requires
o: real-time processing with fixed response deadlines
accepted.x: Real-time operating systems are designed to respond within fixed deadlines, which is essential in such applications.
accepted.tq: Infer the operating-system type from the timing requirement of the application.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Real-time operating system — no response deadline
Batch operating system — jobs run without user interaction after grouping
Time-sharing operating system — one user permanently monopolises the CPU
Distributed operating system — a single isolated machine only
accepted.x: Batch systems group jobs and run them without continuous user interaction. The other options reverse or deny the defining features of their systems.
accepted.tq: Match each operating-system type with its defining operational feature.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: A time-sharing or multi-user operating system is characterised by
o: one job being processed without any scheduling
accepted.x: Time-sharing systems allocate CPU time among multiple users or processes; UNIX is an example.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining feature rather than merely recalling an example.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding mobile operating systems?
o: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google.
Android and iOS are command-line-only systems.
BharOS was developed by a private foreign corporation.
accepted.x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google, while iOS is associated with Apple. BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.
accepted.tq: Use the developer-platform-location distinction to reject swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: BharOS is associated with
accepted.x: BharOS is an Indian mobile operating system associated with IIT Madras.
accepted.tq: Recall the institutional association of a named operating system.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CLI — icons and windows controlled mainly by a mouse
accepted.x: MS-DOS is associated with a command-line interface. GUIs use icons, windows and mouse interaction, as in Windows and macOS.
accepted.tq: Distinguish CLI and GUI by their visible interaction method.
accepted.sec: Operating systems - functions, types, interfaces, examples  [GK]

accepted.s: Which programming-language generation uses mnemonics and requires an assembler for conversion?
accepted.x: Second-generation assembly language uses mnemonics and is converted into machine language by an assembler.
accepted.tq: Match the language generation with its characteristic translator.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Assembly language is a fourth-generation database language.
SQL is a first-generation machine language.
FORTRAN was the first high-level language and appeared in 1957.
accepted.x: FORTRAN is identified as the first high-level language and dates from 1957. SQL is a fourth-generation language used for database queries.
accepted.tq: Combine the language-generation fact with its historical date.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s:
Match the following programmers with the associated language:

a. Dennis Ritchie
a. C++
b. Bjarne Stroustrup
c. James Gosling
d. Guido van Rossum

i. Python
ii. Java
iii. C
iv. C++

Select the correct code:
accepted.x: Dennis Ritchie is associated with C, Bjarne Stroustrup with C++, James Gosling with Java and Guido van Rossum with Python.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive person-language pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compiler from an interpreter?
o: A compiler translates only comments, whereas an interpreter translates only variables.
An interpreter is used exclusively for assembly language.
A compiler translates the whole program at once, whereas an interpreter translates and runs it line by line.
Both always translate only one line at a time.
accepted.x: A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
accepted.tq: Compare paired translators by the unit and timing of translation.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an algorithm?
o: A permanent hardware component inside the CPU
A pictorial symbol used only for decisions
A finite, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem
A storage unit larger than a byte
accepted.x: An algorithm is a finite sequence of ordered steps used to solve a problem or perform a task.
accepted.tq: Identify the formal definition among unrelated descriptions.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a flowchart symbol with its function?
accepted.x: An oval represents start or end; a diamond represents decision, a parallelogram input/output and a rectangle a process.
accepted.tq: Use the symbol-function pair and reject swapped flowchart meanings.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems  [GK]

accepted.s: Pseudocode is best described as
o: an English-like outline of a program or algorithm
accepted.x: Pseudocode expresses program logic in an English-like form without requiring the exact syntax of a programming language.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a planning representation from executable code and hardware.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its number-system base?
accepted.x: Binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal have bases 2, 8, 10 and 16 respectively.
accepted.tq: Check the base rather than the familiar name of the number system.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: The hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆ is equal to
accepted.x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.
accepted.tq: Convert hexadecimal by applying place value and digit value.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: The binary number (1010)₂ is equal to
accepted.x: (1010)₂ equals 8 + 0 + 2 + 0, which is 10 in decimal notation.
accepted.tq: Evaluate binary digits using powers of two.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following gates is a universal gate?
accepted.x: NAND and NOR are universal gates because basic logic functions can be implemented using either of them.
accepted.tq: Recall the special classification of universal logic gates.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: An XOR gate produces output 1 when
accepted.x: For the stated two-input condition, XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ.
accepted.tq: Apply the truth condition rather than confusing XOR with OR.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s:
Consider the following Boolean identities:
1. A + A = A
2. A · A′ = 0
3. (A + B)′ = A′ · B′
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are valid Boolean identities; the third is De Morgan's law.
accepted.tq: Verify each algebraic identity independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]

accepted.s: The laws represented by (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ are associated with
accepted.x: The stated complement relation is De Morgan's law within Boolean algebra, developed in the Boolean tradition associated here with George Boole.
accepted.tq: Identify the named logical law from its algebraic expression.
accepted.sec: Programming and logic - languages, translators, algorithm/flowchart/pseudocode, number systems, logic gates  [GK]
